structured_output.world_model: W5 (contrarian), after E025. Noise: 3-seed SD about 0.25 pp. The tip's (E023) true mean is about 0.753–0.754, so it has essentially no margin. My mechanism: the Lookahead alpha ramp ∝ (step/total)^3 means the final averaged weights come almost entirely from the last ~30% of steps, which run at 32 px. Accuracy is set by the absolute number and quality of 32 px tail steps, plus a smooth bridge from 28 px into them. Uniform epoch cuts (E020, E023) shrink the tail, so they lose accuracy roughly linearly (~2.3 s/pp). E018 lost by removing the bridge. Hyperparameter nudges (LS, Muon lr, wd, alpha exponent) do not change the tail and sit on a ±0.1 pp plateau. Untried lever: cut or downsize the early low-res steps while holding the absolute 32 px step count (and the 28 px bridge) fixed. For example, the 24 px phase gets 70% of its steps, or 22 px at 26 px-equivalent cost, while the 32 px tail stays at ~68 steps. Expect −4–6% time for ≤0.15 pp. Anything that touches the tail (FreezeOut over the tail, bigger batches with fewer tail steps, fewer EMA updates) costs accuracy at about the epoch-dial rate or worse.

forecasts.reason: I038 was discarded, so branch (b): −0.25 epoch saves ~2.5% time. It also shortens the 32 px tail, so expected accuracy is ~0.752, a coin flip against both the 0.753 and 0.7535 bars.

The truncation runs over the 32 px tail that the EMA averages. Group-1 LR reaching 0 by 75% plus frozen early features under the BN-train drift costs more than 0.2 pp. The time saving is about 3–5%, not the full 4% on every run.
Dropping 10% of easy samples on an underfit CIFAR-100 model acts like a ~0.8-epoch cut. It may slightly beat the dial, but 3 seeds can't tell, and the stale low-res loss ranking adds noise.
20% fewer Muon steps with the same lr, and fewer Lookahead updates in the tail, cost ~0.3 pp. The GPU is already saturated at batch 2000, so the time saving is only 2–4%.
With renormalized filters, Muon lr is only an angular step size. This sits on the same plateau as E013/E014/E022/E025, so a ≥0.2 pp held-out gain is unlikely.

cruxes: Is accuracy set by the absolute number of 32 px (EMA-weighted) tail steps? Test: shrink only the 24 px phase (e.g. 90→60 steps) while keeping the 28 px and 32 px step counts fixed. If held-out accuracy stays within 0.15 pp at −5% time, the tail mechanism holds and the best path is cheap early phases, not epoch or architecture cuts.
What is E023's held-out seeds 3–12 mean? If it is below 0.7535, the tip has no margin, and every trim idea (I042–I045) needs an accuracy booster first.
Does the per-step time at batch 2000 still include fixed overhead (Muon NS, the optimizer, the Python loop), so that fewer steps (I044/I045) buy more time than their pixel share suggests?
